title: Acme escalation: nightly sync throttled
summary: Acme's nightly sync in the beta got 429s at about 1,100 requests per second even though D-12 allows a 3,000/s burst: each Envoy node kept its own local bucket, splitting the limit across nodes. Locked D-15: rate-limit buckets live only in the shared gateway Redis cluster, never per node, and T-02: Priya replays Acme's sync at 3,000/s in staging before launch and Rob confirms with Acme.
utterances: Acme's CTO emailed me at 6am. Their nightly sync on the beta got hammered with 429s.
I looked. They were throttled at roughly 1,100 requests per second, well under the burst we agreed in D-12.
So the bucket config is wrong?
Config is right. The problem is each Envoy node runs a local bucket as a fast path. Three nodes, so each one only allowed a third.
So the 3,000 burst became three buckets of a thousand.
Exactly. The local fast path was meant as a cache but it became the limit.
We need one source of truth. Buckets only in the shared Redis cluster, no per-node limits.
Does that hold up the 5 millisecond budget? C-03.
Redis is in the same AZ as the gateway. We measured 0.8 milliseconds p99 for the extra round trip.
Then let's lock it: rate-limit buckets live only in the shared gateway Redis, never per Envoy node.
And before I tell Acme it's fixed I want proof. Priya, replay their sync in staging at 3,000 a second.
I'll replay the real traffic shape from their logs, 60 seconds at 3,000, and share the graph by Monday.

locks.text: Rate-limit buckets live only in the shared gateway Redis cluster, never as per-Envoy-node local buckets, so a tenant's limit is not split across nodes (fixes Acme's throttling under D-12; adds about 0.8 ms p99, within C-03).
Priya replays Acme's nightly sync shape at 3,000 req/s for 60 s in staging and shares the results; Rob then confirms the fix with Acme.
